passage: Democracy is often misunderstood as merely a system where people vote or where a parliament exists. However, a true democracy requires more than just the presence of a legislature or the act of voting. For an election to be considered truly free and fair, it must offer a genuine choice between political alternatives, ensuring that those currently in power have a fair chance of losing. Furthermore, democracy is not simply the rule of the majority. While the majority makes decisions, they must respect the fundamental rights of the minority and operate within the constraints of the law. A government that ignores the rights of individuals or acts outside the legal framework cannot be called democratic, even if it was elected by a large number of people. Ultimately, democracy is a system that protects human dignity and ensures that every citizen has a voice, regardless of their status. It is defined by the rule of law, where the government is accountable to the people and the constitution, rather than the unchecked will of the majority or the mere existence of formal institutions.

items.evidence: For an election to be considered truly free and fair, it must offer a genuine choice between political alternatives, ensuring that those currently in power have a fair chance of losing.
items.q: Everyone in a country can vote, but the ruling party always wins. Why is this election not fair?
options: Voters have no real choice, so rulers cannot lose
Some citizens are kept away from the voting booths
Too many parties compete, which causes instability
Elections are held only once, then rulers stay on
items.explain: A fair election gives a genuine choice and a real chance that those in power lose.

wrong.why: thinks everyone voting makes an election fair
thinks competition for power is harmful
thinks one election is enough for leaders

items.evidence: A government that ignores the rights of individuals or acts outside the legal framework cannot be called democratic, even if it was elected by a large number of people.
items.q: A government wins a big election and then takes away a small group's rights. Is it democratic?
options: No, it ignores the rights of a minority
Yes, because the majority chose it
Yes, because the majority can decide anything
No, because the army must hold final power
items.explain: A government that ignores individual rights is not democratic, even if many people elected it.

wrong.why: thinks majority support justifies any action
thinks the majority can do whatever it wants
thinks unelected officers should hold final power

items.evidence: Democracy is often misunderstood as merely a system where people vote or where a parliament exists.
items.q: Which country shows that having a parliament alone does not make a democracy?
options: One where a parliament exists but rulers ignore the law
One where rulers are chosen in fair, open contests
One where the constitution limits what rulers may do
One where every citizen has a voice in decisions
items.explain: A parliament alone is not enough; a democracy also needs rule of law and accountable rulers.

wrong.why: thinks any country with a parliament is democratic
picks a true feature that does not answer the question
thinks democracy means everyone decides directly

items.evidence: It is defined by the rule of law, where the government is accountable to the people and the constitution, rather than the unchecked will of the majority or the mere existence of formal institutions.
items.q: How does the rule of law protect citizens from their rulers?
options: It makes even top leaders answer to the constitution
It lets ordinary people be judged but not leaders
It lets the majority set aside the constitution
It gives skilled officers the last word on laws
items.explain: Under the rule of law, the government is accountable to the people and the constitution.

wrong.why: thinks top leaders are above the law
thinks the majority's will overrides the law
thinks skilled unelected officers can hold final power
